text:
emma: Heads-up — running long streaming tests in QA and hitting socket exhaustion / flaky failures. App code was creating `new HttpClient()` per request and we also have a Polly retry policy wrapping the call. Anyone seen this pattern cause problems?

raj: Yup. Newing HttpClient per request is classic leak. Use `IHttpClientFactory` or a single static client. Also check MaxConnectionsPerServer.

olivia: +1 to IHttpClientFactory. Also, if you retry a streaming read you need to be careful — the response stream may have been partially consumed and not rewindable.

emma: Ah ok. We're using `HttpCompletionOption.ResponseContentRead` currently. Should we change that?

raj: For streaming scenarios use `HttpCompletionOption.ResponseHeadersRead` and then `response.Content.ReadAsStreamAsync()` and stream manually. That avoids buffering the whole payload. But note: Polly retries are applied before you start consuming the stream. If the retry policy triggers after you start reading, it won't magically restart the body.

matt: If you want retries on transient network errors, configure the Polly policy on the HttpClient handler (via AddHttpClient). Example: 
```csharp
services.AddHttpClient("api", c => {
  c.BaseAddress = new Uri("https://api.example.com");
})
.AddTransientHttpErrorPolicy(p => p.WaitAndRetryAsync(new[] { TimeSpan.FromSeconds(1), TimeSpan.FromSeconds(2) }));
```
This keeps the client pooled and the policy wired in.

olivia: If the endpoint returns a streaming chunked response and you need idempotent retries, you either need the server to support resuming or buffer the streaming payload (tradeoff). For long-lived streams (SSE, event streams) avoiding retries entirely is often simpler; implement reconnection logic at app level.

emma: What about connection pooling settings? We're seeing TIME_WAIT and a lot of sockets in CLOSE_WAIT.

raj: Set `SocketsHttpHandler.PooledConnectionLifetime` or `PooledConnectionIdleTimeout` via `HttpClientHandler`/`SocketsHttpHandler` in the factory config. Also `MaxConnectionsPerServer` if concurrency is high. Example: 
```csharp
services.AddHttpClient("api")
  .ConfigurePrimaryHttpMessageHandler(() => new SocketsHttpHandler {
    PooledConnectionLifetime = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5),
    MaxConnectionsPerServer = 100
  });
```

dev-bot: :robot_face: CI job `integration/streaming-tests` failed 3/8 — see logs at https://ci.redwood.ai/1234

emma: Thanks, I'll switch to IHttpClientFactory, set ResponseHeadersRead, and move Polly to the client registration. Will also add a small buffer for the test runs to avoid flaky partial reads.

matt: One more: when reading the stream use `using var stream = await resp.Content.ReadAsStreamAsync(); using var reader = new StreamReader(stream); while (!reader.EndOfStream) { var line = await reader.ReadLineAsync(); ... }` and avoid calling `.Result` anywhere. Async-only avoids thread starvation.

olivia: If you need per-request policy differences, use named/typed clients instead of creating ad-hoc policies around `SendAsync` calls. Keeps lifetime semantics correct.

emma: Will do. I'll push a small PR and tag you both for review. cc @raj @olivia :thumbsup:

raj: Thanks — ping if you need help with the DI bits.

olivia: Happy to review the PR. Also add a note in the SDK doc about streaming + retry caveats so we don't rediscover this. :memo:

emma: Added a quick note in the PR description and referenced an internal doc link: https://internal.redwood.ai/devex/httpclient-streaming-retries

matt: Nice. Once PR is merged re-run the failing CI job and see if socket counts improve.

emma: Will do in 30m. Thanks everyone. :raised_hands:
